findings.title: Clarify quantitative limits of decomposition controls
findings.prior_acknowledgment: The report already labels control subtractions non-causal and matching approximate. The code and null protocol document identical repeated token vectors. This review makes the consequence for comparability explicit.
findings.finding: The affine null repeats one xA+b across every token and rollout, removing within-answer heterogeneity before nonlinear sparse decomposition. Calibration quality matches minimize uncentered energy mismatch across k, without jointly matching component variance or active atoms. These are counterexamples and diagnostics, not estimates of artifact bias in observed gaps.

evidence.fact: All three matched rotations use k25 against native k10, with active_atoms_mismatch=15 and residual-energy mismatch -0.012183 to -0.009957.

findings.minimal_remedy: Name the identical-token null and approximate calibration-energy matching beside the control table; preserve the current non-causal language.
findings.optional_followup: Distribution-matched affine controls only if seeking to quantify or eliminate sparse-decomposition artifacts.

findings.title: Bring training censoring into the final target-definition paragraph
findings.prior_acknowledgment: Censoring and the differing train/validation versus primary-test completion policy are explicit in generation_coverage_20260913.md and completion_scoring_20260913.md; abbreviated in the final report.
findings.finding: Training and validation retain nonempty length-capped answers while primary evaluation conditions on both models completing all five draws. That difference should accompany the central definition of the learned target.

evidence.fact: All four observed native gap signs survive including all 256 captured test rows; maximum gap change is 0.001522.

findings.minimal_remedy: State the training/validation censoring counts or policy beside the 1024/128/256 split and conditional 252-context evaluation scope.
findings.optional_followup: A refit excluding censored training targets could assess training-policy sensitivity, but is not required for the present descriptive conclusion.

findings.title: Distinguish numerical lens stability from answer-state construct validation
findings.prior_acknowledgment: The plan calls train-domain calibration an approximation; the report qualifies R-space as operational and the intervals as conditional on calibrated dictionaries.
findings.finding: Calibration uses raw prompt prefixes and qualitative readouts on calibration prompts. Matrix/direction stability and forward/backward checks do not establish stability of answer-state sparse assignments or component gaps under a new calibration draw. This does not demonstrate that current gaps are unstable.

evidence.fact: 119 valid calibration prompts and 29 qualitative readout positions per model; even/odd cosine approximately 0.992-0.998, relative Frobenius differences approximately 0.070-0.127.

findings.minimal_remedy: Label the demonstrated stability as prompt-calibration matrix/direction stability and explicitly leave answer-state component stability unmeasured.
findings.optional_followup: Evaluate component stability under independent or answer-domain calibration before broadening beyond the present operational dictionary.
